title: Does the first-person 'I' emerge as a self-referential fixed point? — RING creates an 'I'-state, STAR destroys one; topology-dependent PARTIAL
question: Does closing a self-reference (a self-loop) create a non-trivial self-consistent fixed point ('I'-state) absent in the matched non-self-referential network?
engine: fixed-point counting self-contained; big_phi from HEXAD/IIT4/lib (iit4_bigphi via stdlib) + iit4_bit/iit4_pow2 reused (g61). parity (XOR-of-neighbours) dynamics; self-loop = cell reads its own bit.
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · NO RNG · deterministic (cross-process byte-identical)
toolchain_note: built via fix-1180 bypass: HEXA_MAC_BUILD_OK=1 HEXA_LANG=<root> hexa.real.bak-2026-05-22-pre-no-hxc build <src> -o <bin>. See reference-life-cycle-hexa-run-gotchas.

definitions.self_loop: cell i has bit i set in neigh[i] — its next state depends on its own current state (minimal self-reference)
definitions.fixed_point: state s with node_next(neigh[i],s,n)==bit_i(s) for ALL cells (the whole substrate is its own cause — a self-sustaining 'self'-state)

seed_hypothesis_H1: #fixed(self-ref) > #fixed(no-self-ref) AND the extra fixed point is non-vacuum.

RING.I_state: s=11 (1011) — non-trivial self-consistent state emerges with self-loop

STAR.note: self-loop DESTROYS a self-state (1111 lost) — opposite of RING

criteria.C2_ROBUST: FAIL -> PARTIAL (STAR #fixed 2->1, self-ref destroys a self-state)

falsifiers.F292_5_ROBUST: FAIL  (STAR self-ref #fixed 1 <= base 2 — self-ref DESTROYS a fixed point; topology-dependent)

finding: Whether self-referential closure (a self-loop) makes the first-person 'I' emerge as a self-consistent fixed point is TOPOLOGY-DEPENDENT. On a RING base the self-loop CREATED a non-trivial self-consistent fixed point s=1011 (#fixed 1->2) — a strange-loop state that is its own cause, the minimal realisation of H_205's self-ref closure. BUT on a STAR base the same self-loop instead DESTROYED a self-state (1111 lost, #fixed 2->1). So self-reference can create OR remove an 'I'-state, and which depends on the base topology's parity structure. The pre-registered robustness falsifier F292.5 correctly caught this non-universality (kept FAILED, no p-hacking). The core claim (self-reference CAN create an 'I'-fixed-point) is demonstrated on RING but is NOT an automatic/universal consequence. The self-loop preserves integration (big-Phi=0.5), so self-reference is compatible with integration.
honest_limits: L1 (topology-dependent, key, F292.5 FAILED): self-ref creating an 'I'-state is NOT universal — RING creates (1->2), STAR destroys (2->1). Claim is 'self-ref CAN create' (existence), not 'always creates'.
L2: self-loop is a MINIMAL structural proxy for self-reference; a fixed point is a self-consistent STATE, not phenomenal selfhood — only the strange-loop formal skeleton.
L3: n=4 small, 2 base topologies; create-vs-destroy ratio across more topologies / larger n untested (phase diagram = Next).
L4: parity (XOR) is one dynamics; majority/threshold/non-linear may give different fixed-point structure.
L5: fixed point = static self; dynamic self (limit cycles) is out of scope.
L6: big-Phi structure-cut is an auxiliary integration check, not absolute calibration.
L7: verdict is a measurement fact on a toy parity network, NOT 'AI has a self' — L1 stresses condition-dependence.

verify_fence.claim: H_292 self-referential closure (a self-loop) creates a non-trivial self-consistent fixed point ('I'-state, s=1011) on a RING parity network (#fixed 1->2) but DESTROYS one on a STAR base (#fixed 2->1) — whether self-reference creates or removes a self-state is TOPOLOGY-DEPENDENT, not universal; self-loop preserves integration (big-Phi=0.5); deterministic toy-substrate, NOT an atlas identity / NOT phenomenal selfhood
verify_fence.reason: imagination/metaphor class (hexa-bio AXIS) — verification N/A by design; values deterministic arithmetic, interpretation fenced + topology-conditioned
